children: An ad-fraud group known as MoldyRoost used programmatic advertising and disguised landing pages to launch automated exploit attacks against vulnerable iPhones, according to cybersecurity firm Confiant. According to PANews, clicking an ad and loading a malicious landing page could trigger an attack without requiring a download or further action. From May 12 to November 17, the group was linked to more than 480 advertising domains, with attacks reported in at least 47 countries and regions. The exploit toolkit was used to steal seed phrases for MetaMask, Phantom and Trust Wallet, as well as keychain data, messages and photos. The report said the attack chain mainly targeted older iOS versions, and Apple fixed some DarkSword vulnerabilities in iOS 26.3.

title: MoldyRoost Used iPhone Exploit Chain to Steal Crypto Wallet Seed Phrases
